items.label: f04-uncertain-commit
items.front: What is an uncertain commit, and the safe response?
items.back: An error after COMMIT was sent but before the acknowledgement arrived. Retry the same idempotent request - the key makes the retry safe, which is the payoff of the design.

items.label: f01-cancel-boundary
items.front: MeterForge cancellation: what does checking the token before work guarantee, and what doesn't it?
items.back: A request cancelled before insertion writes nothing. Cancellation after a successful store cannot erase it, so a lost response still needs a same-key retry: 'the client cancelled' is not 'the server did not commit'.

items.label: f03-why-move-to-db
items.front: What is the actual reason to move MeterForge's idempotency store from memory to a database?
items.back: The unique constraint survives restarts and covers every replica; the in-memory store forgets keys on restart and cannot coordinate two API instances.

items.label: f02-immutable-record
items.front: Why does UsageEvent have getter-only properties, given the store is a ConcurrentDictionary?
items.back: The dictionary coordinates only the key-to-record mapping; immutability protects the record after publication. A mutable list inside a thread-safe dictionary would need its own synchronization.
